{{Quote|I am a simple merchant, my Queen. A Jedi released me from the prison after I tried to organize a group of freedom fighters.|The merchant, upon meeting Queen Padmé Amidala|audio=ImASimpleMerchant.flac|<ref name="TPM game" />}}
A [[Naboo (people)/Legends|citizen]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], a [[Human/Legends|Human]] '''merchant''' was [[Prisoner/Legends|imprisoned]] by the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] during its [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|invasion]] of the planet in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]. According to the [[Merchant/Legends|merchant]], the arrest was a result of attempting to organize a [[Naboo Resistance|resistance group]] against the invaders.

While inside the cell, the merchant was found by the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], who was on a mission to rescue Naboo's [[Monarch of Naboo/Legends|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]]. The merchant was released by the Jedi, and he later assisted Amidala in the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|liberation]] of the planet by giving her a stash of stockpiled weapons.

==Biography==
===Prisoner of the Trade Federation===
{{Quote|Um, ya&hellip; you see, the Trade Federation, th&hellip; they captured me when I tried to organize resistance against this&hellip; this terrible invasion!|The merchant, explaining the predicament to Obi-Wan Kenobi|audio=TheyCapturedMe.flac|<ref name="TPM game" />}}
A [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Merchant/Legends|merchant]] was a [[Naboo (people)/Legends|resident]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] and was present on the planet when it was [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|invaded]] by the [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|droid forces]] of the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]]<ref name="TPM game" /> in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates the events of the film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']] to [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]. The same timeline placement applies to the film's [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|video game adaptation]], which features the [[Merchant/Legends|merchant]].</ref> The individual was captured by the Trade Federation and was put in a [[Prison/Legends|prison]] in the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Theed/Legends|Theed]], although the merchant managed to sneak in a [[Thermal detonator/Legends|thermal detonator]].<ref name="TPM game" />

{{GameMechanics|legends=1|Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' video game}}
[[File:E1_game_prisoner.jpg|thumb|left|275px|The merchant thanks Obi-Wan Kenobi for releasing him.]]
A short [[Time/Legends|time]] later, [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]]&mdash;who was on a mission to escort [[Monarch of Naboo/Legends|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] of the Naboo to her [[J-type 327 Nubian royal starship/Legends|starship]] in order to escape the invading forces&mdash;stumbled upon the [[Prisoner/Legends|imprisoned]] merchant. The merchant pleaded to Kenobi to be set free, claiming to have been incarcerated for trying to organize a [[Naboo Resistance|resistance cell]] against the invaders.<ref name="TPM game" />

Although Kenobi initially suspected that the prisoner may have been a criminal, he believed the merchant's words and released the latter. The merchant then gave Kenobi the thermal detonator as a reward and advised him to use it on the Federation [[Armored Assault Tank/Legends|Armored Assault Tank]] that was blocking the way to the [[Theed Hangar/Legends|hangar]] housing the [[Queen/Legends|queen's]] [[Starship/Legends|ship]]. As the Jedi departed, the merchant made a promise to Kenobi about seeking people to fight the Trade Federation [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]].<ref name="TPM game" />

===Amidala's return===
{{Quote|Good luck, my Queen!|The merchant, to Queen Padmé Amidala|audio=GoodLuckMyQueen.flac|<ref name="TPM game" />}}
After Kenobi and the queen fled the planet, the merchant began stockpiling weapons to combat the Trade Federation. During this time, the individual heard the news that Amidala had supposedly been [[Death/Legends|killed]] offworld by agents of the Federation, and was saddened by the loss of the queen. Eventually, the Naboo and their allies, the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] [[Species/Legends|species]], launched a joint attack to [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|liberate]] their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]].<ref name="TPM game" />

As a battle was raging throughout Theed, the merchant stood on a balcony near the same cell in which the individual had previously been imprisoned. There, the merchant encountered Amidala herself, who was alive and had returned to the planet, personally leading the assault on Theed. The merchant informed Amidala of the earlier encounter with Kenobi and provided the queen with a stash of stockpiled weapons, including a [[proton missile launcher]] and ten [[Flash grenade/Legends|flash-bang grenades]]. As Amidala turned to leave, the merchant wished her luck in the liberation of the planet, which soon proved successful.<ref name="TPM game" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Oh, help me! You gotta let me out! I've been wrongfully imprisoned!|The merchant begs to be released by Obi-Wan Kenobi|audio=WrongfullyImprisoned.flac|<ref name="TPM game" />}}
[[File:MerchantMeetsQueen.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The merchant meets with Queen Amidala.]]
Upon meeting with Obi-Wan Kenobi, the merchant was very nervous, pausing between phrases and requiring time to find needed words. At first, Kenobi did not believe the merchant's story and suspected that the individual may have lied and could actually be a criminal. Even after Kenobi had released the individual, the merchant still continued to insist on innocence, claiming to ideally be viewed as a hero and urging Kenobi to "[[Force sense/Legends|sense]] the truth."<ref name="TPM game" />

However, by giving Queen Amidala the stockpiled weapons, the merchant proved to be at least truthful about working toward the liberation of Naboo. The merchant was delighted to see the queen alive, after hearing rumors that she had been killed. The merchant had [[Color/Legends|light]] skin, gray [[Hair/Legends|hair]], a gray-white beard, and brown [[Eye/Legends|eyes]].<ref name="TPM game" />

==Equipment==
{{Quote|What are you doing?''"<br />"''I've been stockpiling weapons in preparation for a revolution against the Trade Federation!|Queen Padmé Amidala and the merchant|audio=IveBeenStockpilingWeapons.flac|<ref name="TPM game" />}}
During the Invasion of Naboo, the merchant wore an [[Clothing/Legends|outfit]] consisting of a brown [[Jacket/Legends|coat]], brown pants, and black [[Boot/Legends|boots]]. While imprisoned, the merchant was able to keep a thermal detonator, which was later given to Kenobi as a reward. After being liberated, the merchant began stockpiling weapons to fight the Trade Federation, amassing an arsenal that included at least ten flash-bang [[Grenade/Legends|grenades]] and a [[Proton torpedo/Legends|proton]] [[Missile launcher/Legends|missile launcher]]. The merchant readily supplied those weapons to Queen Amidala, hoping that they would help her in the struggle to liberate the planet.<ref name="TPM game" />
{{Endgame}}

==Behind the scenes==
The Naboo merchant appeared in the [[1999]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' video game]], developed by Big Ape Productions and published by [[LucasArts]]. The merchant was credited as "Prisoner" and was voiced by [[Tom Kane]],<ref name="TPM game" /> one of the most prolific ''[[Star Wars]]'' voice actors.<ref name="Kane">{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/news20081003b.html|text=Tom Kane: Mastering Yoda}}</ref>

As in-game [[Easter egg (virtual)|Easter eggs]], the game's development team made several [[Wikipedia:Non-player character|NPCs]] look like real-world celebrities. This particular merchant was given the appearance of actor [[Wikipedia:Sean Connery|Sean Connery]],<ref name="Q&A">{{WebCite|url=http://www.lucasforums.com/showthread.php?t=5630&page=5|text=TPM Q & A - Page 5|author="[[Ray West (3D artist)|Zanzibar]]"|date=2001-08-13, 4:51 AM|work=[https://archive.is/bVr5 LucasForums]|quote=Congrats to Jedi72, you got 'em!|archiveurl=https://archive.is/UfaYE}} {{C|In response to: "Sean Connery - Escape from Theed level. He's the one in that is locked in the room. You have to walk down some stairs to reach his cell. When you free him he offers you a detonator."}}</ref> famous for his roles in the [[Wikipedia:Production of the James Bond films|''James Bond'' film series]] and the film [[Wikipedia:Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade|''Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade'']].<ref name="Connery roles">{{WebCite|url=https://seanconnery.com/filmography|text=Filmography|work=[https://seanconnery.com SeanConnery.com]|archivedate=20241206131427}}</ref> Following the release of the game, this Easter egg was confirmed during a Q&A session<ref name="Q&A" /> with Big Ape Productions' 3D Modeler/Animator, [[Ray West (3D artist)|Ray West]],<ref name="TPM game" /> going under the alias "Zanzibar," on a fan forum dedicated to LucasArts video games.<ref name="Ray West identity">{{WebCite|url=http://www.lucasforums.com/showthread.php?t=5607|text=Real or Fake?|author="[[Ray West (3D artist)|Zanzibar]]"|date=2000-10-16, 6:14 PM|work=[https://archive.is/bVr5 LucasForums]|quote=Yeah, it's real, I sent it in merely as a response to a review rather than an 'interview' tho I can't remember who I sent it to.|archivedate=20150927062028}} {{C|In response to: "I'm Ray West, the 3d artist/animator for Big Ape Productions, the team that produced Star Wars: Episode 1 - The Phantom Menace for Lucasarts. [&hellip;] Zanzibar, is this real or another kid playing a prank?"}}</ref>

===Alternate paths===
[[File:KenobiMurderer.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The merchant is killed by Obi-Wan Kenobi.]]
There are a number of alternate ways that the fate of the merchant can unfold in the game. The individual can first be encountered as a non-playable character in the fifth level of the game, titled "Escape from Theed," in which the player controls Obi-Wan Kenobi. Since the encounter does not affect the game's storyline, the meeting with the merchant can be avoided entirely. If the merchant is encountered, the player can either leave the merchant inside the cell or release the individual. In the latter scenario, it is also possible for the merchant to be killed right afterward.<ref name="TPM game" />

Unless the prisoner has been killed by Kenobi, the player&mdash;this time controlling Queen Amidala&mdash;can once again encounter the merchant in the tenth level, titled "Assault on Theed." If Kenobi did not encounter the merchant previously or chose to keep the individual locked up, then the prisoner will still be located inside the cell. Amidala will then have the same options available to her, and she can either ignore the merchant's pleas and leave the individual imprisoned, can release and then kill the merchant, or she can release the merchant and let the individual live. However, if the prisoner has already been released by Kenobi, then Amidala will encounter the merchant on a balcony outside the individual's cell, and the merchant will provide her with weapons. This article currently follows the latter version of events.<ref name="TPM game" />

Due to a glitch in the game, if Amidala releases the merchant, lets the individual run to the waiting spot at the balcony, and then kills the merchant, a new version of the merchant will respawn right next to the dead body. This copy will then act out the dialogue corresponding to the scenario in which the merchant was released by Kenobi.<ref name="TPM game" />
